name: Migrate records between systems with Claude-assisted mapping and validation

parameters.content:
## Migrate records between systems with Claude-assisted mapping and validation

Ops and engineering teams moving data from one CRM, help desk or database to another without a migration vendor.

### How it works
Trigger: Each phase — profile, map, validate, dry-run, cutover — starts on an explicit click; no phase runs unattended.
1. Profile the source
2. Propose the mapping
3. Confirm the mapping
4. Apply transformations
5. Validate
6. Dry run
7. Cut over in batches
8. Reconcile and hand over
Every AI step is followed by a "Needs a person?" gate that parks low-confidence items; the write-back waits for an approval.

### Setup
1. Open "Config (edit me)" and fill in the fields (names, approver, quiet hours, thresholds).
2. Add credentials: Anthropic, plus Postgres / BigQuery, Target APIs (HubSpot, Salesforce, Zendesk…).
3. Run once with test_mode on, read the output, then switch the trigger on.

### Customization tips
Put the source and target schemas in the Config node; run each phase (profile, map, validate, dry-run, cutover) by hand from the manual trigger.
Guardrail to keep: No phase runs without an explicit trigger; cutover requires a dry run that passed.

Full blueprint: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/data-migration-automation/

## Trigger and config
The entry point and the one node you edit: names, approver, quiet hours, test mode.

## 1. Profile the source
Tables, fields, types, null rates, distinct values and sample rows from the source system (database, CRM export, API)

## 2. Propose the mapping
Reads source and target schemas with sample values and proposes field-by-field mappings with transformation notes (date formats, picklist translation, splits/merges) and a confidence per field

## 3. Confirm the mapping
The mapping sheet is reviewed and edited by the migration owner; it becomes the versioned source of truth for every later step

## 4. Apply transformations
Transformations generated from the mapping sheet — type conversions, lookups, deduplication rules — applied to a sample batch

## 5. Validate
Record counts, sums of numeric fields, referential integrity and picklist coverage compared between source and transformed target sample; failures listed per rule

## 6. Dry run
Full transformed dataset loaded into a target sandbox; reconciliation report produced; errors per batch

## 7. Cut over in batches
Production load in batches with progress, per-record error capture and retry; the source stays read-only during cutover

## 8. Reconcile and hand over
Final reconciliation report, error log, the mapping sheet and the rollback procedure archived; the workflow can re-run deltas for late data

## Fill this in first
Every later node reads these values. Keep test_mode on for the first week.

Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- Source system (database, CRM/helpdesk export or API)
- Target system API or import
- Mapping sheet (owner-confirmed)
- Validation rules

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Propose the mapping" step of the Data Migration Automation workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Reads source and target schemas with sample values and proposes field-by-field mappings with transformation notes (date formats, picklist translation, splits/merges) and a confidence per field.

Rules:
- No phase runs without an explicit trigger; cutover requires a dry run that passed.
- The mapping is confirmed by a person; the agent proposes with confidence, it does not decide.
- The source is read-only during cutover and a tested rollback exists before the first production batch.
- Every transformed record carries its source id for traceability.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

nodes.name: Needs a person?
nodes.notes: True = the AI step was not sure or flagged the item → dead letter, a person looks. False = continue. Wire the dead letter to a Slack message or a sheet so nothing fails silently.
